title: US tech stocks see sharp falls over AI cost concerns

claims.claim: Intel shares fell as much as 30% after the chip maker warned of a weaker computer market and increased spending on AI.

evidence.quote: Shares in Intel continued their overnight slide into early trading on Friday, falling as much as 30% after the chip maker warned of a weaker computer market even as it plans to increase spending on AI.

claims.claim: Amazon shares fell as far as 6% after its reported earnings on Thursday evening fell short of investors' expectations.

evidence.quote: Amazon shares fell as far as 6% before recovering after its reported earnings on Thursday evening fell short of investors' expectations.

claims.claim: The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock exchange opened on Friday down 2.5% at its lowest level in more than two months.

evidence.quote: The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock exchange opened on Friday at its lowest level in more than two months, down 2.5%, as other tech stocks including Reddit and Roblox continued to fall.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq stock exchange opened on Friday at its lowest level in more than two months, down 2.5%

claims.claim: Google owner Alphabet plunged by more than $500bn in value on Thursday after revealing AI summaries affected its core search advertising revenue.

evidence.quote: The losses follow the value of Google owner Alphabet plunging by more than $500bn on Thursday after it revealed its own AI summaries were affecting its core search advertising revenue.

claims.claim: Alphabet stock continued to fall in early trading on Friday, down 1%.

evidence.quote: Alphabet stock continued to fall in early trading, down 1% after Thursday's massive slide.

claims.claim: Intel was on track to lose more than $130bn in value following its earnings update.

evidence.quote: The bigger losses on Friday were elsewhere, with Intel on track to lose more than $130bn in value after its earnings update rattled investors.

claims.claim: Intel's finance chief David Zinsner stated on Thursday that the firm did not expect positive cash flow this year and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for the fourth quarter.

evidence.quote: On Thursday, Intel's finance chief David Zinsner said the firm did not expect positive cash flow this year, and forecast lower-than-expected revenue for its fourth quarter.

claims.claim: David Zinsner stated that the PC slowdown is expected to continue at least through the first half of next year.

evidence.quote: "Looking ahead, we see the PC slowdown continuing at least through the first half of next year," he said in the chip maker's third quarter earnings report.
